title: Hachar pitches Webb County a former bank as its new tax office: lease it, skip the build
excerpt: Miguel Hachar offered Webb County a 10-year lease-to-own deal on the former Texas Community Bank branch at 1101 San Bernardo Ave. as a ready-made tax office, an alternative to building a new one. Commissioners took no action.
content:
A local developer has offered Webb County a ready-made tax office: the former Texas Community Bank branch at 1101 San Bernardo Ave., a roughly 12,000-square-foot building that could house the county tax assessor-collector instead of a new building the county has been planning, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Miguel Hachar of Hachar Realty Group presented the proposal to county commissioners on Wednesday, pitching the building as a turnkey solution. He said it is ready for immediate use — “It’s ready to move in tomorrow,” he said — and includes 12 teller windows, a vault, a drive-thru and an estimated 150 parking spaces, plus room for a small sheriff’s substation.

The offer is a 10-year lease-to-own agreement, with the county able to buy the building at the end of the term and two five-year renewal options, Hachar said. His group would pay for all renovations and improvements and keep the building up to code and maintained. He said the county could put the savings toward other needs, such as roads. No lease price or purchase figure was stated.

The pitch is an alternative to building a new tax office near the new justice center on Guadalupe Street. On November 3, commissioners approved a $25,000 contract for a feasibility study of that proposed complex. The county recently bought the former BBVA building at 300 Convent Ave. for use as a tax office annex, and had also planned a new tax office at 1000 Houston St.

Commissioners took no action on the offer during the presentation. County Judge Tano Tijerina said no decision has been made and the feasibility study is still ongoing, adding that the county is reviewing all options with taxpayers in mind. Commissioner Rosaura “Wawi” Tijerina said the county is open to the proposal and noted the time it would save over waiting for a new building to be constructed. She suggested the county engineer’s office review the offer.

The former bank branch has been closed for years and empty for about a decade, Hachar said. The current tax office is on Houston Street, with about 1,500 square feet more than the bank building, according to the Morning Times.

Sources:

  • Laredo Morning Times, "Hachar pitches Webb County on former bank facility," November 12, 2026
